question: Does transactional local evaluation state recover from process loss while preventing superseded attempts and stale inputs from authorizing current success?
primary_metric: All eight case invariants hold in all three replications; current effective decisions replay exactly from retained transactional events and raw attempt records.

case_acceptance.claim_race: 32 current passes, exactly one claim/committed attempt per job under four processes
case_acceptance.death_after_claim: Process exits 23 after claiming; recovery reaches one current pass with token 2
case_acceptance.transaction_rollback: Process exits 24 inside an uncommitted write; state remains pending and recovery commits token 1
case_acceptance.acknowledgement_loss: Process exits 25 after committing; restart retains token 1 and one current pass
case_acceptance.late_completion: After lease expiry and replacement, old completion is fenced, new token 2 owns the sole current decision
case_acceptance.stale_reuse: Changed source disables a completed pass at export; the original passing attempt remains retained
case_acceptance.stale_pending: Changed enrollment is invalidated before grading; no attempt is executed
case_acceptance.retry_budget: Three expired claims exhaust the job with retry_exhausted and no candidate success

historical_integration: One pre-fix and fixed revision for each of the two locked historical tasks. Kill one claimant before grading, then recover with four workers; all four calibrated outcomes must match and exactly one job must need a second token.
abort: Abort on any mismatch, audit failure or 600-second wall budget; preserve failed artifacts. Do not retune or replace failed runs under this protocol.
claim_limit: Same-host SQLite coordination and process fault injection on trusted CPU graders. Execution may repeat; only a current fenced terminal decision is deduplicated. No network partition, distributed fleet, machine power-loss, OS containment or model-learning result. Kill points occur before grader launch or after commit, not during a hostile child process.
